clue.text: Seafood dish locals start promoting

indicators.note: to dish something is to ruin or wreck it, so the word locals is knocked into a new order
the start of promoting is only its opening letter

explanation.surface: A seafood dish is being pushed by the local residents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seafood dish' reads as one phrase, but 'dish' is the anagram signal: LOCALS rearranged gives SCALLO, then P from 'start promoting'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bivalve with a fan-shaped shell is a familiar shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: One who may buy sec-end jumper

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a hopper is something that hops or jumps

explanation.surface: A customer might pick up a second-hand sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a British sweater, but here it is literally a thing that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopper is a customer, someone out to make purchases.

clue.text: Exhausted after a time, got dressed

indicators.note: after puts the exhausted word behind a and time

parts.note: tired means exhausted

explanation.surface: Worn out after a while, someone finally put clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Attired is a formal word for clothed.

clue.text: Nothing reverts to Queen Elizabeth II for example?

definitions.text: Nothing reverts to Queen Elizabeth II for example?

indicators.note: reverts means the word for nothing turns back on itself

parts.note: nil means nothing
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A remark that nothing goes back to the late monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen Elizabeth II, or QE2, was a famous ocean liner; 'Queen' gives ER while the whole phrase defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The QE2 was a Cunard passenger ship, an instance of an ocean-going vessel.

clue.text: Cat's paw tread with care

parts.note: pussy is an informal word for cat
an animal's foot

explanation.surface: A cat's paw steps delicately.
explanation.definitionFit: To pussyfoot is to move warily or act cautiously, like a stalking cat.

clue.text: Grumble about watch

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover protecting the glass

explanation.surface: Someone moans about having to keep watch.
explanation.walkthrough: A HUNTER is a pocket watch with a metal lid; 'chunter' is British informal for muttering complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: To chunter is a British colloquialism for muttering complaints, i.e. grumbling.

clue.text: Start research into fuel growth undersea

indicators.note: into puts the letter inside the fuel word

parts.note: coal is a fuel

indicators.note: the start of research is its opening letter only

explanation.surface: Begin investigating fuel growing on the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is built up by colonies of marine polyps on reefs beneath the sea.

clue.text: Last to speak on Tom's breakdown

parts.note: to utter is to speak

indicators.note: a breakdown breaks the letters of Tom's apart into a new order

explanation.surface: The final word on Tom's nervous collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom's' supplies four letters, S included, which 'breakdown' rearranges to MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttermost means furthest or extreme, as in the farthest or final point.

clue.text: City's investment in actor on tour

indicators.note: an investment is something put in, so the answer is clothed within these words

explanation.surface: A city's money backs a performer on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is 'has'; the city is invested, clothed, in actor on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada.

clue.text: It makes the holes for Batman's opponent

definitions.meaning: something that riddles, i.e. pierces with holes
the puzzle-setting villain of the Batman comics

explanation.definitionFit: To riddle is to perforate, and the question-mark-clad supervillain fights Batman.

clue.text: Trips that got us in trouble

indicators.note: the words got us in are troubled, stirred up into a different order

explanation.surface: Excursions that landed the group in a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' reads as a phrase, but 'in' is fodder and 'trouble' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Outings are short excursions or jaunts, the same as trips.

clue.text: Left work and went to bed

definitions.meaning: stopped working for good at the end of a career

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both giving up employment at pension age and withdrawing to sleep.

clue.text: Description of beam in doorway

indicators.note: in tells us the beam is placed inside the doorway word

parts.note: a portal is a grand doorway or gate
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: An account of a shaft of light falling through an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a depiction or representation, an account of something.

clue.text: No time for hire of organ

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: relating to an organ

indicators.note: No here says the letter for time is to be left out of the hire word

parts.note: a rental is a hire, as in car rental

explanation.surface: Hiring a church organ leaves no time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' sounds like the church instrument; here it is the kidney, and 'of organ' is an adjectival definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal means relating to the kidneys, which are bodily organs.

clue.text: Broadcast advertisement in city

indicators.note: in signals that the advertisement goes inside the city name

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city, often just Rio

explanation.surface: A commercial is aired in an urban area.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio is broadcasting by sound waves, used as an adjective or noun for broadcast.

clue.text: Choosing to include time for working

indicators.note: to include means the choosing word takes the time word inside it

parts.note: opting means choosing
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Picking to make room for time at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is running or functioning is said to be in operation.

clue.text: Not on the green, nor in the pink

definitions.meaning: read literally: not on, i.e. away from, the colour green
in good health; preceded by nor it means not well

explanation.walkthrough: 'nor' links the two and negates the second: not in the pink means unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, being away from a hue; idiomatically, feeling slightly ill, the opposite of healthy.

clue.text: Prudence in a scrap, gets awfully sore

indicators.note: gets means receives, so the scrap takes in the other letters

parts.note: a scrap is a fight

indicators.note: awfully means the letters of sore are badly mangled

explanation.surface: Showing care in a brawl leaves someone terribly sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a scrap' looks like being in a fight; 'in' is only a link, and 'gets' is the container signal while 'awfully' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight is planning ahead wisely, the forethought that makes up prudence.

clue.text: Front-man for the current monarch

parts.note: present means current, existing now
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A spokesman acting for the reigning sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current monarch' reads as one phrase about the reigning sovereign, but it splits into two pieces, with 'for the' merely linking them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A TV host who fronts a programme is called its front man.

clue.text: Bill, mountain climbing with Jack perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the mountain word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: an Alp is a mountain
the jack is a playing card

explanation.surface: Bill scaled a peak with his friend Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' and 'Jack' look like two names; Bill is a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a printed notice posted publicly, as in bill-posting.

clue.text: Intellectual talk-it protects the viewer

indicators.note: talk indicates the word is spoken, with the H dropped

parts.note: a highbrow is an intellectual

explanation.surface: Clever chatter shielding the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken without its H, HIGHBROW sounds like EYEBROW; the viewer is the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The ridge of hair above each eye shields it from sweat and debris.

clue.text: Wax and wane

definitions.meaning: a slender wax candle or spill
to grow gradually smaller or thinner

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a thin candle and also means to narrow off towards an end.

clue.text: Stick out assignment

definitions.meaning: a piece of set work or scheme

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to jut forward; the noun is a planned task or school assignment.

clue.text: Train and join up in case of resistance

indicators.note: in places the reversed join word inside the case
the case of resistance is its first and last letters
in a down clue up means the word reads backwards

parts.note: to unite is to join

explanation.surface: Train and unite to put up resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a verb paired with 'join up', but it is the noun definition; 'up' reverses the joining word in this down clue, and 'case of' gives the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the body of attendants following an important person, like a bride's train.

clue.text: Point in the region of the sports ground

indicators.note: in places the point inside the word for region

parts.note: an area is a region or zone
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Somewhere near the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the region of' looks like 'about', but here 'in' is the container signal and 'region' gives AREA.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed stadium where sports and events are staged.

clue.text: Home team dismissed completely

parts.note: in means at home
a side is a team in sport
out, as a batsman dismissed in cricket

explanation.surface: The home side were bowled out entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a dismissed batsman is OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing something thoroughly is an idiom for knowing it fully.

clue.text: Bull's Head in meal with no starter

indicators.note: with no starter means losing the opening letter

parts.note: dinner is a meal

explanation.surface: A bull's head served at a meal minus the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course; here it is the first letter. On a dartboard or target the inner is the ring next to the bull.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target, the ring just around the bullseye is the area at the head of the bull.

clue.text: Investigate origins of locked van in river

indicators.note: in puts the letters inside the river name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: origins means the opening letters of locked and van

explanation.surface: Look into how a locked van ended up in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig into or research something thoroughly.

clue.text: Accuse Scottish island harbouring returning US serviceman

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering inside, so the island holds the serviceman

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: returning means the serviceman's letters are read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A Scottish islander is charged with hiding an American soldier coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: Arran lies off Scotland's west coast; GI is the standard term for an American soldier, and 'returning' turns it round before 'harbouring' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to call someone before a court to answer a charge.

clue.text: Ship's log — alone, dis heartened, abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild or unrestrained, so the letters are let loose into a new order
disheartened here means losing the heart, the central letter of alone

explanation.surface: A captain's log records being left alone, dejected and deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes the middle O from ALONE, giving ALNE; with LOG these letters are rearranged by 'abandoned'.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large sailing vessel of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: Old lady's party bet

parts.note: a do is a party or social event
a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: An elderly woman's gamble at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title from her late husband, typically elderly.

clue.text: Mad hatter began to enjoy performance

indicators.note: mad here means the letters of hatter go crazy into a different order
began to means only the beginning letter of enjoy is used

explanation.surface: A crazy milliner started having fun at the show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland is a decoy: 'Mad' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre can mean dramatic performance as an art, as in a night of fine theatre.
